Moon Phase Calculator
The Moon's phase and illumination on any date, computed astronomically.

How the phase is calculated

The Moon goes through a full cycle of phases every 29.53 days, from new moon to full moon and back. The calculator measures how far a chosen date is from a known new moon and works out where in that cycle it falls, then shows the phase name and the percentage of the Moon that is lit.

This is an astronomical approximation, accurate to within about a day, which is right for most purposes. For the exact moment of a new or full moon, check the Panchang.

Moon phases and the Hindu calendar

Phases matter in Indian tradition because the lunar calendar is built on them. The waxing half of the month is Shukla Paksha and the waning half is Krishna Paksha, and observances such as Purnima and Amavasya fall on the full and new moons. The Panchang turns this into the tithi for each day.

Frequently asked

Common questions

What is the difference between a moon phase and a tithi?

A phase describes how much of the Moon is lit. A tithi is one of 30 lunar days, defined by the angle between the Sun and the Moon, and it is what the Panchang uses for festivals and muhurat.

Can I find the Moon phase on the day I was born?

Yes. Enter your date of birth and the calculator shows the phase and illumination for that day.

How accurate is it?

It is based on the average length of the lunar cycle, so it is reliable to within about a day. For exact times, use the Panchang.
